name: Minesweeper
hint: Every board can be solved without a guess, Hint shows the next step and why, and Odds shows every tile's chance of a mine. Right-click (or long-press) to flag; click a number to open around it.
alt: Minesweeper: a grass field half opened by the computer player, numbers and flags on sand

name: Flappy Bird
hint: Space, click or tap to flap. Crashed? Rewind (Z) the last seconds, see the path that hit, and fly on from there. Press C for today's course and race the ghost of your best run.
alt: Flappy Bird: the teal bird in flight between copper pipes

name: Dino Game
hint: The dinosaur game and the old bot that played it by watching one pixel. Press E to breed bots that do better.
alt: Dino Game: a generation of evolving bots, colored dinosaurs jumping together, the best one solid with its red jump eye and blue duck eye

name: NathaNOS
hint: A fake desktop with icons, a start menu and a taskbar: open any other app, or paint pixel pictures in its own Paint that land on the desktop as icons and can become the wallpaper.
alt: NathaNOS desktop

name: Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe
hint: Nine boards; your cell picks your opponent's next board, and pointing at one shows which. New to it? How to play (L) teaches the rules in six moves on the real board. Then play the computer or a friend by link, and review every move.
alt: Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe: a game under way between two computer players, one board won by X

name: Rubik's Cube 2D
hint: Learn to solve it, even your own: paint in your real cube's colors (C) or Mix one, then Teach me (T) shows every turn, layer by layer. Or make famous patterns with it (G), from a checkerboard to the superflip, one guided turn at a time, or play 20 levels for stars. Cubers: the Timer (K) gives scrambles, times your solves with Space and keeps your Ao5 and Ao12.
alt: Rubik's Cube 2D window with the 3D cube

name: Synthesizer Keyboard
hint: Learn five songs as the next key lights up, playing the keys or singing, whistling or playing a real instrument to the microphone. Chord keys (Q) turn every key into its chord. Record a tune and send it as a link, or loop two bars of your playing into a band of four layers.
alt: Synthesizer Keyboard: the looper playing a melody and a bass layer

name: Clock
hint: The analog, digital or flip clock with a brass alarm hand you drag to set, plus a timer you set by dragging its red dial (it keeps counting in another tab, then rings) a stopwatch with laps, focus sessions (25 minutes, then a break), and a world clock that finds the hours that suit everyone for a call.
alt: Clock: the World tab, a 24-hour dial with a hand for here, London, New York and Tokyo over a strip of hours for each city

name: Sprite Floaty Stars
hint: Orbits: click to place up to four suns and a thousand stars fall round them, trailing light. Sky writing: type a message and the stars swoop in to spell it. Plus Star Catcher, six nights of gold stars to catch, and the five original star fields to pull in and fling.
alt: Sprite Floaty Stars: Orbits, a thousand stars circling three suns

name: Number Guess
hint: Find the hidden number in five ranges, from 1-10 to 1-1,000,000. The number line lights what is still possible: type a guess or click it. Par or better is three stars. Duel races the computer: you each hide a number from 1 to 100 and take turns hunting the other, fewer guesses wins. You pick turns it around: the computer guesses yours, even if you lie once. Magic is a card trick: say which of six cards hold your number and it reads your mind, then shows how.
alt: Number Guess: a duel against the computer, each lane narrowing in on the other's hidden number

name: Tank Game
hint: Tank duel against the computer or a friend, behind walls that change every round, racing for parachuted supply crates: shields, triple shots, ricochets. W A S D and Q drive and fire red (or hold the mouse or a finger to drive, tap to fire), arrow keys and M green. First to three rounds wins.
alt: Tank Game: a red and a green tank fighting among concrete walls on grass

name: Music Theory Expert
hint: Ear training in six drills, a Songwriter that loops chord progressions from a circle of fifths while you play a melody over them, and a Chord finder: hold any notes and it names the chord, writes it on a staff and finds its key.
alt: Music Theory Expert: the Songwriter, a circle of fifths beside the chords of G major and a keyboard

name: Circle Spawner
hint: Builds circles, hearts, stars, words, a ticking clock and your own drawings (even flipbook cartoons) out of borderless windows that morph from shape to shape. Drag one to fling the whole shape like a jelly, click one to scatter it, or press Spin to turn it round like a coin.
alt: A rainbow clock showing the time, built out of windows under the Circle Creator window

name: Screen Saver
hint: Ten screen savers, from the original green circles to an aquarium of fish that stay yours (a new one moves in each day you look in, and F feeds them) and a brick maze walked in first person. G shows all ten at once, live, to pick one; T lets the mouse or a finger play with the saver instead of closing it; 9 for the fish, 0 for the maze, N for the next.
alt: Screen Saver: a painted aquarium with named fish among swaying weed

name: Windows
hint: An on-screen Windows key that stays on top: click it for Start, hold it and press a key for Win+that key, or slide off it to snap a window; its ▴ opens a shelf of every shortcut to tap. Here it plays on a pretend Windows whose Start menu holds every app on the site: type to search, Enter to play.
alt: Windows: a Start menu of every app on the site, with the on-screen Windows key beside it

name: Windows+E
hint: A keyboard of Windows shortcuts: Win+E as many times as you ask opens that many File Explorer windows, and Win+D, Win+R, Win+Tab and the arrows hide, run, list and snap them. Add steps to press a list in a row: Side by side opens two windows on the two halves. A little monitor shows what it will do first, and Preview plays it there without pressing a key. Here they play on a pretend Windows over this site's app folders: double-click a folder to play it.
alt: Windows+E: its keyboard of Windows shortcuts, with the Side by side steps listed and a little monitor showing them done, in front of two File Explorer windows snapped side by side

name: Bible Downloader
hint: Now a Bible reader: an open book in five public domain translations, any two side by side verse by verse; press G and type a passage (jn 3:16, ps 23) to open it, with reading plans (the Gospels in 30 days up to the Bible in a year) that set a short reading each day on a calendar you fill in. Highlight a verse, then learn it by heart one first letter at a time, with reviews that come back tomorrow, in 2 days, 4, 8. Press D for night pages, cream ink on a dark page under a lamp. Still saves chapters as web pages.
alt: Bible Downloader: Luke 1 open as a two-page book with a red ribbon bookmark

name: Stock Checker
hint: A practice trading desk: $10,000 of play money in a simulated market that opens at its last real 2016 quotes, against four computer traders. Click the chart to set a buy or sell line that trades by itself, or press H to hear the chart. B buys, S sells, R shows the race, Space pauses.
alt: Stock Checker trading desk: a watch list with sparklines beside a day chart and buy and sell buttons

name: Group Creator
hint: Deals a class into random groups, then remembers every round so the next one gives people partners they have not had yet. A chart shows who has met whom, and a spinning wheel picks whose turn it is, everyone once before anyone twice. A roll call sits out who is away today and keeps chosen pairs apart, and every member gets a role that rotates round by round.
alt: Group Creator: groups dealt onto cards

name: Simple Algorithms
hint: Algorithm Lab: race six sorting algorithms, hear them work and see each whole run as one picture, draw a maze and watch A*, Dijkstra and three more searches find the way, see a Tower of Hanoi solve itself from the binary of each move, and square roots and sine converge, or be the sort yourself: weigh look-alike boxes two at a time.
alt: Simple Algorithms: Algorithm Lab window
